maya: Heads up — nightly TP all-reduce regression. Saw ~12% tail latency increase on multi-GPU runs when seq_len distribution has a heavy tail. Repro on 8xA100, TP=4, pipeline=2.

maya: Narrowed to message size cluster around ~48KB. Perf trace shows lots of small inflight fragments rather than few large transfers. Suspect comm coalescing + kv-cache interaction.

joel: Can you paste the profiler output (nccl timelines / cublas overlap)?

maya: Pasted short excerpt from perf:

```
# nccl timeline sample (simplified)
allreduce chunk_id=42 size=49152us start=1200us end=2040us stall=180us inflight_frags=7
allreduce chunk_id=43 size=51200us start=2060us end=2905us stall=210us inflight_frags=9
kv_cache: flush(prefix)=true generations=3 coalesced_msgs=2
kernel_autoswitch: selected=tree heur=comm_stride(8192) -> tree
```

maya: The "inflight_frags" spikes line up with KV prefix flushes. When prefix cache hits, we emit many small KV-prefixed msgs, which prevent NCCL from forming fewer larger transfers.

sasha: Interesting. We recently landed the kernel gating change that biases toward tree if comm_stride < 16KB. If fragments are ~48KB but interleaved by small kv msgs, the runtime sees stride noise and picks tree, which increases number of small AllReduce rounds.

liam: That gating change is my CL: https://phabricator/redwood/D12345 — it was meant to avoid ring stalling on very small steady-state msgs, but maybe it misfires with bursty kv patterns.

dena: Can you run a quick A/B? Disable prefix caching or force ring and compare p50/p95?

maya: Did both: disabling prefix cache (env REDWOOD_KVCACHE_PREFIX=0) drops inflight_frags by ~60% and p95 improves ~9%. Forcing ring (RUNTIME_FORCE_NCCL=ring) also improves but increases p50 slightly.

perf-bot: CI job tp-allreduce/8gpu-nightly #342 failed with latency regression +12% (linked run: https://ci.redwood/342) :eyes:

joel: So two levers: 1) make kernel selection robust to interleaved small control msgs (raise comm_stride hysteresis or add smoothing), 2) add transient coalescing window for kv-prefixed msgs so they get merged if following an allreduce chunk. Both have tradeoffs.

sasha: Proposal: introduce a 1ms coalescing window for KV flush messages when there is recent allreduce activity, and adjust comm_stride to be percentile-based (20th/80th) over last N chunks instead of instant value. Prototype plan in branch tp/commstride-smoothing.

liam: Sounds good. Also add a perf counter for "coalesce_opportunity_misses" so we can measure effectiveness.

dena: Quick note — be careful with the coalescing window on low-latency workloads (RPCs). Maybe restrict to TP allreduce path only.

maya: I'll run a microbenchmark: run_local_tp_perf.sh --tp=4 --seq-dist=zipf --prefix-cache=on/off --force-ring=on/off. Pasted run results: 

```
# bench summary (8gpus, tp=4)
config A (prefix on, autoswitch): p50=12.1ms p95=28.3ms inflight_frags_avg=6.8
config B (prefix off):          p50=12.4ms p95=25.8ms inflight_frags_avg=2.7
config C (force ring):          p50=12.8ms p95=26.1ms inflight_frags_avg=3.1
```

maya: TL;DR prefix+autoswitch gives best p50 but worst p95. Coalescing should recover p95 without hurting p50 much.

joel: If you push the prototype, I'll run full nightly suite and measure end-to-end. Also add kernel selection unit tests that simulate interleaved small msgs.

sasha: I'll spike it later today. Assigning to myself, will post branch and test plan. :rocket:   

maya: Thanks — please tag me. Also add dashboard card under TP-allreduce to visualize msgsize histogram and inflight_frags. :eyes: :chart_with_upwards_trend:   

liam: FYI we should also backport a config flag for Dedicated customers who might want to tune the hysteresis.

dena: Good call.

perf-bot: Created issue perf/TP-commstride-2023 with baseline numbers.

maya: Great work team — short follow-ups: sasha prototype, joel nightly run, liam config flag, maya will update dashboard.

sasha: I'll send the branch link when ready.

maya: :thumbsup:
